<task_result>
# Project inspection report

## Executive summary

`C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai` is a **single-page, multi-provider AI marketing assistant** branded “Oxy AI.” Its intended purpose is marketing research, copy/campaign planning, web research, clarification questionnaires, and eventual execution against advertising/productivity platforms through Composio.

The core chat and tool-streaming MVP is substantially implemented: users can choose an AI model, stream a response, invoke web-search/fetch tools, answer structured clarification questions, render Markdown, and stop or restart a conversation. However, it appears to be an **in-progress prototype rather than a production-complete application**. Most notably:

- Composio “execution” is explicitly a stub and does not execute actions.
- There is no authentication, user/account model, conversation persistence, rate limiting, or database.
- A provider-filtering models endpoint exists but is not used by the UI.
- No application tests or test script exist.
- The README is still the default Create Next App text.
- TypeScript passes, but ESLint currently fails in an apparently unused UI primitive.
- The unrestricted server-side URL fetcher presents an SSRF risk if publicly deployed.

Inspection excluded:

- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\open-agents`
- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\chatbot-template`
- Generated/dependency trees such as `.next` and `node_modules`

The root TypeScript configuration itself also excludes the two reference trees at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\tsconfig.json:25-33`.

---

## What the application is

The strongest product definition comes from:

- Metadata: “Oxy AI — Marketing Agent” and “AI marketing execution — web search via Exa, questions, and Composio integrations” at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\layout.tsx:19-22`.
- Empty-state description: “Marketing execution agent — search the web with Exa, clarify with questions, and execute via Composio” at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx:58-78`.
- Server system prompt: a marketing execution assistant for copy, research, campaign ideas, and tool-driven actions at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api\chat\route.ts:65-80`.

The current UI is a focused chat surface rather than a broader marketing dashboard. There are no campaign-management pages, analytics screens, saved workspaces, integration settings, or account pages.

---

## Routes

Only three application routes were found:

| Route | Implementation | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /` | `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\page.tsx:1-6` | Renders the chat and passes the static model list. |
| `POST /api/chat` | `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api\chat\route.ts:18-90` | Validates the model/messages, runs the AI/tool loop, and streams UI-message events. |
| `GET /api/models` | `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api\models\route.ts:4-21` | Returns the hard-coded models, filtered by configured providers when any provider key exists. |

There are no dynamic chat routes, auth routes, integration callbacks, persistence endpoints, admin endpoints, loading/error route boundaries, or health endpoints.

### Unused models route

The page directly imports and passes `MODELS` at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\page.tsx:1-5`. No caller of `/api/models` was found. Consequently, its configured-provider filtering at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api\models\route.ts:7-18` currently has no effect on the actual model selector.

---

## Main user flows

### 1. Start a conversation

On first load, the user sees an empty state and four prompt suggestions:

- Tell a richly formatted story
- Search for current DTC marketing trends
- Plan a campaign, with clarification first
- Ask about Composio integrations

Evidence: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\suggestions.tsx:5-24`.

Selecting a suggestion immediately submits it with the current model at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx:69-76`.

The story suggestion is generic rather than marketing-specific, suggesting some demo/scaffolding residue.

### 2. Choose a provider/model and send prompts

The bottom prompt form provides:

- Multiline text entry
- Enter-to-send and Shift+Enter for a newline
- Model selection
- Send button
- Stop-generation button while busy

Evidence: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\prompt-form.tsx:30-90`.

The selector receives a static list and displays model names at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\model-select.tsx:24-49`.

The initial client model is always `models[0]` at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx:29-41`, which is GPT-4o in the hard-coded list at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\models.ts:11-18`.

### 3. Stream an assistant response

`useChat` owns the current client conversation and status at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx:32-43`. The UI:

- Shows “Thinking…” while submitted.
- Streams assistant message parts.
- Displays a destructive alert on request failure.
- Allows cancellation through `stop()`.

Evidence: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx:81-140`.

User messages are rendered as right-aligned bubbles, while assistant messages dispatch individual text/tool parts to specialized renderers at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat-message.tsx:20-67`.

Assistant text supports Markdown and GitHub-flavored Markdown via `react-markdown` and `remark-gfm` at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\parts\text-part.tsx:1-14`.

### 4. Clarification questionnaire

The model can call `ask_user`, which requires one or more questions with exactly three choices each at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\ask-user.ts:4-23`.

A pending questionnaire appears as a sticky card above the prompt area:

- Choice selection
- Free-form “another answer”
- Multiple-question progress
- Previous/next navigation
- Required-field validation
- Final submission

Evidence: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\question-card.tsx:29-85`.

The client posts the answer as tool output and automatically resumes the conversation once the tool call is complete at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx:32-37` and `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx:105-116`.

### 5. Web research

The model has two active web tools:

- `exa_search`
- `web_fetch`

Search progress/results are rendered as result cards with title, snippet, and external link at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\parts\exa-search-part.tsx:5-70`.

Fetched pages show success/failure state, HTTP status, content type, truncation state, and a preview at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\parts\web-fetch-part.tsx:5-66`.

AI SDK `source-url` parts, when supplied, are deduplicated and shown in a side drawer at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\parts\sources-part.tsx:25-99`.

### 6. Composio integration discovery/action attempt

The model can:

- List marketing/productivity apps.
- Request a generic app/action/parameter combination.
- Display action status through a Composio-specific tool card.

Registration: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\index.ts:6-13`.

Rendering: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\parts\composio-part.tsx:4-46`.

In practice this is currently discovery/simulation, not live execution; see “Completion status.”

### 7. Start over and change theme

“New Chat” navigates to `/` with a regular anchor, causing a full reload and clearing the in-memory conversation at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\new-chat-button.tsx:5-12`.

The theme defaults to the system theme and can be toggled with the unmodified `D` key when the user is not typing at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\theme-provider.tsx:6-20` and `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\theme-provider.tsx:37-68`.

---

## Architecture

### Technology stack

This is a single-package application using:

- Next.js 16 App Router
- React 19
- TypeScript with strict mode
- Tailwind CSS 4
- shadcn/Base UI primitives
- Vercel AI SDK 7 and `@ai-sdk/react`
- `react-markdown` with GFM

Versions and dependencies are declared at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\package.json:11-43`. There is no separate backend package or monorepo application architecture in the inspected root project.

### Server/client split

- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\layout.tsx` and `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\page.tsx` are server components.
- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx` is the main client boundary.
- Provider resolution and all network tools run in server-side route/tool code under `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api` and `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai`.
- Provider and integration secrets are read from server environment variables rather than exposed to the client.

### Request/data flow

1. The user submits text plus the selected model from `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx:131-138`.
2. The default `useChat` transport targets the chat API.
3. `POST /api/chat`:
   - Parses JSON.
   - Applies a default model if absent.
   - Rejects models outside the whitelist.
   - Resolves the provider and checks its key.
   - Validates all UI messages against the registered tool schemas.
   - Converts UI messages to provider/model messages.
4. `streamText` runs the provider with all five tools.
5. Stream events are converted back to AI SDK UI-message parts.
6. The client renders text, tool calls, tool results, and sources.

Evidence: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api\chat\route.ts:18-64` and `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api\chat\route.ts:83-89`.

The agent loop is bounded to five steps, 8,192 output tokens, and a 30-second route duration at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api\chat\route.ts:14-16` and `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api\chat\route.ts:58-64`.

### UI organization

The active feature components are:

- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx`
- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat-message.tsx`
- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\prompt-form.tsx`
- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\model-select.tsx`
- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\question-card.tsx`
- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\suggestions.tsx`
- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\site-header.tsx`
- `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\new-chat-button.tsx`
- Tool renderers under `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\parts`

There is also a large catalog of reusable primitives under `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\ui`, many of which are not used by the current chat screen. `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\hooks-chatbot` contains only `.gitkeep`.

---

## AI and provider integrations

### Language-model providers

Four providers and 14 hard-coded models are supported:

- **OpenAI:** GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, GPT-5, GPT-5 mini
- **Anthropic:** Claude Sonnet 4, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.6, Haiku 4.5
- **Google:** Gemini 2.5 Pro, 2.5 Flash, 2.0 Flash
- **OpenRouter:** three hard-coded `:free` models

Evidence: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\models.ts:1-100`.

Provider setup:

- Native OpenAI adapter
- Native Anthropic adapter
- Native Google Generative AI adapter
- OpenRouter through the OpenAI-compatible API at `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`

Evidence: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\provider.ts:1-4` and `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\provider.ts:57-97`.

Provider clients are cached in memory by API key at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\provider.ts:28-69`.

Required configuration is documented at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\.env.example:3-14`:

- `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
- `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`
- `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
- Optional `EXA_API_KEY`
- Optional `COMPOSIO_API_KEY`

### Search

With `EXA_API_KEY`, the tool uses `exa-js` `searchAndContents`, requesting summaries, up to 3,000 characters of text, and fallback live crawling at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\exa-search.ts:118-148`.

Without an Exa key, it scrapes DuckDuckGo’s HTML endpoint with regular expressions at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\exa-search.ts:32-93`. This makes search usable without a key, but HTML scraping is inherently brittle.

An additional `exaSearchSimpleTool` exists at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\exa-search.ts:159-200`, but it is not registered in `getTools()` and is therefore dead code in the current application.

### URL fetching

`web_fetch`:

- Accepts HTTP/HTTPS URLs.
- Follows redirects.
- Has a 15-second timeout.
- Supports simple text or Markdown-like extraction.
- Limits returned content to 1,000–50,000 characters, defaulting to 20,000.

Evidence: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\web-fetch.ts:4-32` and `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\web-fetch.ts:44-125`.

The HTML conversion is regex-based rather than a DOM/readability parser, so extraction quality will vary.

### Composio

The source explicitly calls this integration a stub at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\composio.ts:4-6`.

Without a key it returns a “would have executed” simulation at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\composio.ts:18-25`.

With a key it:

1. Loads the Composio SDK.
2. Looks up raw tools for the requested app.
3. Reports that the action was found.
4. Returns the discovered tools.

It does **not** call an action execution API. The comments identify the missing `entityId`/user-context flow, and the success response explicitly says user context is still needed at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\composio.ts:28-50`.

Thus the metadata/system prompt’s “execute via Composio” claim currently exceeds the implementation.

---

## Persistence and authentication model

### Authentication

No application authentication model was found:

- No auth routes or middleware/proxy exist in the root application.
- No auth dependency appears in `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\package.json:11-32`.
- No server session, user ID, organization, role, or permission checks occur in either API route.
- Composio has no per-user `entityId` or connected-account association.

Therefore, if deployed publicly, `/api/chat` would be an unauthenticated endpoint spending the operator’s provider keys.

### Persistence

There is no product-data persistence:

- No database or ORM dependency.
- No schema or migration directory.
- No conversation repository or persistence endpoint.
- No local/session storage for chats.
- No conversation IDs or dynamic `/chat/[id]` routes.

The transcript lives in the current `useChat` React state at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx:29-37`. Each API request receives and validates the current message array at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api\chat\route.ts:47-61`, making the server effectively stateless. Reloading or pressing “New Chat” loses the conversation.

Theme preference may be persisted internally by `next-themes`, but chats, model choice, users, and marketing actions are not.

---

## Completion assessment

### What appears functional

- Single-screen responsive chat UI
- Multi-provider model routing
- Streaming responses
- Message validation
- Tool-call loop
- Exa/DDG search
- URL content fetching
- Structured clarification questions
- Markdown/GFM rendering
- Tool-specific progress/result UI
- Stop generation and error display
- Light/dark theme

A read-only TypeScript check using `tsc --noEmit --incremental false` passed without errors.

### Evidence that it is in progress

1. **Version is `0.1.0`** at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\package.json:2-4`.
2. **README is untouched Create Next App documentation**, with no product/setup/architecture documentation: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\README.md:1-36`.
3. **Composio is a non-executing stub**, despite being a core product claim.
4. **Provider filtering is unwired.** `/api/models` exists, but the UI receives all static models directly.
5. **Initial-model bug:** the UI starts with GPT-4o regardless of configured providers. A deployment configured only for Anthropic, Google, or OpenRouter will initially select an unavailable OpenAI model and return the missing-key error. Relevant evidence:
   - Static all-model prop: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\page.tsx:1-5`
   - First-model selection: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\chat.tsx:29-41`
   - GPT-4o first in list: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\models.ts:11-18`
6. **Demo behavior is intentional:** `/api/models` returns every model when no keys exist, even though chat will fail at execution, at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\app\api\models\route.ts:5-18`.
7. **No tests or test script.** Scripts only cover dev/build/start/lint at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\package.json:5-10`; no application test files were found.
8. **Lint is not clean.** Targeted ESLint reports `react-hooks/purity` because `Math.random()` is called during render at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\ui\sidebar.tsx:648-651`. That sidebar appears unused by the active product, but it still prevents a clean repository-wide lint.
9. **Dead/unused code exists**, including:
   - `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\components\parts\web-search-part.tsx`
   - `exaSearchSimpleTool` in `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\exa-search.ts:159-200`
   - `getModelById` in `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\models.ts:108-110`
   - `ReasoningPart` type in `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\index.ts:26`
10. **Production essentials are absent:** authentication, persistence, billing/usage controls, rate limits, integration OAuth/callbacks, human approval for irreversible actions, telemetry, tests, and operational documentation.

### Security/operational concern

`web_fetch` only checks that a URL uses HTTP or HTTPS, then fetches it server-side and follows redirects at `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\ai\tools\web-fetch.ts:44-59`. It does not reject localhost, private networks, link-local addresses, cloud metadata endpoints, or redirects into those ranges. This is a likely **SSRF vulnerability** in a public deployment.

The unauthenticated `/api/chat` endpoint also has no rate limiting or usage quota, so public users could consume the application owner’s provider credits.

## Overall verdict

This is a **coherent, type-correct AI chat/tool MVP with a polished component layer**, but it is **not a complete marketing-execution product and is not production-ready**. Web research and clarification flows are real; live marketing-platform execution, identity, persistence, provider-aware onboarding, safeguards, and operational quality remain unfinished.
</task_result>

# chatbot-template A minimal chatbot template built with Next.js, the [AI SDK](https://ai-sdk.dev), [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com), [shadcn/react](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/react/message-scroller), [shadcn/typeset](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/typeset) and the [Vercel AI Gateway](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway).

## Features - Streaming chat with markdown rendering and shadcn/typeset - Tool calling example - Web search via each provider's built-in search tool - Human-in-the-loop questionnaire. The model can ask clarifying questions, answered with the shadcn questionnaire component ## Deploy [![Deploy with Vercel](https://vercel.com/button)](https://vercel.com/new/clone?repository-url=https%3A%2F%2Fgithub.com%2Fshadcn-ui%2Fchatbot-template&project-name=chatbot-template&repository-name=chatbot-template) That's it — no configuration needed. Vercel deployments authenticate to the AI Gateway automatically via OIDC, and usage runs on your team's [AI Gateway credits](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/pricing). ## Local development ```bash pnpm install ``` Then give the app a gateway credential, either by pulling an OIDC token from your linked Vercel project: ```bash vercel link vercel env pull ``` or by creating an API key in the Vercel dashboard (**AI Gateway → API Keys**) and adding it to `.env.local`: ```bash cp .env.example .env.local # then set AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY=... ``` Start the dev server: ```bash pnpm dev ``` ## Configuration | Env var | Required | Description | | -------------------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | | `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` | Local dev only | AI Gateway API key. Not needed on Vercel deployments (OIDC). | The model list lives in [lib/models.ts](lib/models.ts) — the first entry is the default model. ## Security The `/api/chat` route is **public and unauthenticated** — every request spends your AI Gateway credits. That's fine for a personal demo, but before putting it in front of real traffic you should: - **Rate limit it.** Add [Vercel Firewall / WAF](https://vercel.com/docs/security/vercel-waf) rules or [`@upstash/ratelimit`](https://github.com/upstash/ratelimit-js) so a single client can't drain your credits (denial-of-wallet). - **Cap spend.** Set an [AI Gateway spend limit](https://vercel.com/docs/ai-gateway/observability-and-spend/budgets) as a backstop. - **Add auth** if the chatbot isn't meant to be public. The route already validates the request body, restricts models to [lib/models.ts](lib/models.ts), caps output tokens and step count, and aborts generation on client disconnect — but those bound a single request, not overall volume. ## How it works - [app/api/chat/route.ts](app/api/chat/route.ts) streams responses with `streamText` - [components/chat.tsx](components/chat.tsx) renders the conversation with `useChat` and shadcn chat primitives. - [tools/](tools) defines the tools — one file per tool (the filename is the model-facing tool name), composed in [tools/index.ts](tools/index.ts): a server-executed GitHub repo lookup, the interactive `ask_user` questionnaire, and provider-native web search. ## Tool parts Assistant messages are a list of typed parts. [components/chat-message.tsx](components/chat-message.tsx) switches on `part.type` and delegates each one to a component in [components/parts/](components/parts): | Part type | Component | Renders | | ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `text` | [text-part.tsx](components/parts/text-part.tsx) | Markdown via react-markdown and shadcn/typeset. | | `tool-github_repo` | [github-repo-part.tsx](components/parts/github-repo-part.tsx) | A spinner while the lookup runs, then a linked stat line (stars, forks, language). | | `tool-web_search` | [web-search-part.tsx](components/parts/web-search-part.tsx) | A "Searching the web…" status while the search runs, then a persistent "Searched the web" line per search. | | `tool-ask_user` | [ask-user-part.tsx](components/parts/ask-user-part.tsx) | The answered questions inline. Pending questions render in [question-card.tsx](components/question-card.tsx), pinned to the scroller bottom. | | `source-url` | [sources-part.tsx](components/parts/sources-part.tsx) | Web search citations, deduped into a "Searched N websites" drawer once the message finishes streaming. | Tool parts move through states as the stream progresses — `input-streaming` → `input-available` → `output-available` (or `output-error`) — and each component switches on `part.state` to show progress, results, and failures. ### Adding your own tool 1. Create `tools/.ts` (the filename is the model-facing tool name) exporting a `tool()` with a `description`, an `inputSchema`, and an `execute` function (omit `execute` for tools the user answers in the UI, like `ask_user`), then register it in [tools/index.ts](tools/index.ts). 2. Add a part component in [components/parts/](components/parts) and a `case "tool-"` in [chat-message.tsx](components/chat-message.tsx). Message types are inferred from the tool definitions via `InferUITools`, so `part.input` and `part.output` are fully typed in your part component — renaming a tool field is a build error, not a silent `undefined`. ## Adding components ```bash npx shadcn@latest add button ``` ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# AGENTS.md

This file provides guidance for AI coding agents working in this repository.

**This is a living document.** When you make a mistake or learn something new about this codebase, add it to [Lessons Learned](docs/agents/lessons-learned.md).

## Quick Links

- [Architecture & Workspace Structure](docs/agents/architecture.md)
- [Code Style & Patterns](docs/agents/code-style.md)
- [Lessons Learned](docs/agents/lessons-learned.md)

## Database & Migrations

Schema lives in `apps/web/lib/db/schema.ts`. Migrations are managed by Drizzle Kit.

**After modifying `schema.ts`, always generate a migration:**

```bash
bun run --cwd apps/web db:generate   # Creates a new .sql migration file
```

Commit the generated `.sql` file alongside the schema change. **Do not use `db:push`** except for local throwaway databases.

Migrations run automatically during `bun run build` (via `lib/db/migrate.ts`), so every Vercel deploy — both preview and production — applies pending migrations to its own database.

### Environment isolation

Neon database branching is enabled in the Vercel project settings. Every preview deployment automatically gets its own isolated database branch forked from production. This means preview deployments never read or write production data. Production deployments use the main Neon database.

## Commands

```bash
# Development
bun run web            # Run web app

# Quality checks (REQUIRED after making any changes)
bun run ci                                 # Required: run format check, lint, typecheck, and tests
turbo typecheck                            # Type check all packages

# Linting and formatting (Ultracite - oxlint + oxfmt, run from root)
bun run check                              # Lint and format check all files
bun run fix                                # Lint fix and format all files

# Filter by package (use --filter)
turbo typecheck --filter=web # Type check web app only

# Testing
bun test                                              # Run all tests
bun test path/to/file.test.ts                         # Run single test file
bun test --watch                                      # Watch mode
bun run test:verbose                                  # Run tests with JUnit reporter streamed to stdout (useful in non-interactive shells)
bun run test:verbose path/to/file.test.ts             # Same verbose output for a single test file
```

**CI/script execution rules:**

- Run project checks through package scripts (for example `bun run ci`, `bun run --cwd apps/web db:check`).
- Prefer `bun run <script>` over invoking tool binaries directly (`bunx`, `bun x`, `tsc`, `eslint`, etc.) so local runs match CI behavior.

## Git Commands

- **Branch sync preference:** When bringing in `origin/main`, prefer a normal merge (`git fetch origin main` then `git merge origin/main`) instead of rebasing, unless explicitly requested otherwise.

**Quote paths with special characters**: File paths containing brackets (like Next.js dynamic routes `[id]`, `[slug]`) are interpreted as glob patterns by zsh. Always quote these paths in git commands:

```bash
# Wrong - zsh interprets [id] as a glob pattern
git add apps/web/app/tasks/[id]/page.tsx
# Error: no matches found: apps/web/app/tasks/[id]/page.tsx

# Correct - quote the path
git add "apps/web/app/tasks/[id]/page.tsx"
```

## Architecture (Summary)

```
Web -> Agent (packages/agent) -> Sandbox (packages/sandbox)
```

See [Architecture & Workspace Structure](docs/agents/architecture.md) for details.

## File Organization & Separation of Concerns

- Do **not** append new functionality to the bottom of an existing file by default.
- Before adding code, decide whether the behavior is a separate concern that should live in its own file.
- Prefer creating a new colocated file for distinct concerns (components, hooks, utilities, schemas, data-access helpers, etc.).
- If a file is already large or handling multiple responsibilities, extract the new logic (and related helpers/types) into focused modules and import them.
- For large page/view/client components, default to adding new feature behavior in colocated hooks and colocated child components instead of growing the main file.
- If a change introduces a distinct cluster of state, effects, handlers, API calls, or derived UI labels for one feature, treat that as a strong signal to extract it.
- Keep each file focused on one primary responsibility; avoid mixing unrelated UI, business logic, and data-access code in the same file.

## Code Style (Summary)

- **Bun exclusively** (not Node/npm/pnpm)
- **Files**: kebab-case, **Types**: PascalCase, **Functions**: camelCase
- **Never use `any`** -- use `unknown` and narrow with type guards
- **No `.js` extensions** in imports
- **Ultracite** (oxlint + oxfmt) for linting and formatting (double quotes, 2-space indent)
- **Zod** schemas for validation, derive types with `z.infer`

See [Code Style & Patterns](docs/agents/code-style.md) for full conventions, tool implementation patterns, and dependency patterns.

# Open Agents

This repository is based on Vercel's upstream Open Agents project:

- Upstream repo: https://github.com/vercel-labs/open-agents

This fork keeps the same general product idea and architecture, but is adapted to run without Vercel infrastructure.

## What changed from upstream

This fork replaces the Vercel-specific infrastructure pieces with locally runnable alternatives.

### 1. AI Gateway was replaced with direct model provider access

Instead of routing model calls through Vercel AI Gateway, this repo talks directly to model providers.

- OpenAI via `OPENAI_API_KEY`
- Anthropic via `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`
- OpenRouter via `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` (provides access to `z-ai/glm-5.1`, `moonshotai/kimi-k2.6`, and `minimax/minimax-m2.7`)

You can provide any combination of keys. At least one is required if you want to run the agent.

See [https://openrouter.ai/](https://openrouter.ai/) for details on obtaining an OpenRouter API key.

### 2. Vercel Sandbox was replaced with Daytona

Instead of using Vercel Sandbox for the coding environment, this repo uses [Daytona](https://www.daytona.io/). 

Daytona provides the sandbox container where the agent can:

- read and write files
- run shell commands
- install dependencies
- start dev servers
- expose preview ports

### 3. Everything is wrapped in Docker Compose

This repo includes a `docker-compose.yml` that starts the app and all required local infrastructure together.

That includes:

- the Open Agents web app
- PostgreSQL for the app
- Daytona API, runner, proxy, and supporting services

The goal is to make local startup a single command instead of requiring Vercel services.

## Architecture

The core shape is still the same:

```text
Web -> Agent -> Sandbox
```

- `apps/web`: Next.js app and API routes
- `packages/agent`: agent runtime and tools
- `packages/sandbox`: sandbox abstraction and Daytona integration

## Running locally with Docker Compose

### Prerequisites

- Docker
- Docker Compose
- At least one model provider key:
  - `OPENAI_API_KEY`, or
  - `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or
  - `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`

### 1. Export your API key

Example:

```bash
export OPENAI_API_KEY=your_openai_key
```

or:

```bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your_anthropic_key
```

or:

```bash
export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=your_openrouter_key
```

You can also put these in a local `.env` file that Docker Compose will read.

### 2. Start the stack

```bash
docker compose up -d --build
```

This starts the full local stack, including Daytona.

### 3. Open the app

Open:

- `http://localhost:3000`

Useful local endpoints:

- Open Agents web app: `http://localhost:3000`
- Daytona preview proxy: `http://localhost:4000`

### 4. Stop the stack

```bash
docker compose down
```

If you also want to remove volumes:

```bash
docker compose down -v
```

## Local development notes

- Local Docker Compose enables auth bypass for easier local testing.

## In One Sentence

**Oxy AI is a prototype marketing-focused AI chat agent built by extending `chatbot-template`; it borrows the broader tool-using agent idea from `open-agents`, but it is not a full Open Agents implementation.**

## What It Does

The application provides a single conversational interface where users can:

- Chat with models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and OpenRouter.
- Search the web through Exa, with DuckDuckGo as a no-key fallback.
- Fetch and summarize content from URLs.
- Answer structured clarification questions generated by the model.
- Discover and attempt marketing actions through Composio.
- Render streamed Markdown responses, tool progress, search results, and sources.

## Recommendation

Use the native **Node test runner** for the root project. It is the lightest option and requires no new dependency.

The installed Node is **v24.14.0**, whose built-in TypeScript stripping successfully loaded the root’s `.ts` modules. `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` are also covered by the installed `@types/node` **20.19.43**.

Suggested layout:

- Guard: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\runtime-guards.ts`
- Colocated test: `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\lib\runtime-guards.test.cjs`
- Eventual script: `"test": "node --test \"lib/**/*.test.cjs\""`

Example:

```js
const test = require("node:test");
const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
const { isRuntimePayload } = require("./runtime-guards.ts");

test("accepts a valid payload", () => {
  assert.equal(isRuntimePayload({ messages: [] }), true);
});

test("rejects malformed runtime values", () => {
  assert.equal(isRuntimePayload(null), false);
  assert.equal(isRuntimePayload({}), false);
  assert.equal(isRuntimePayload({ messages: "invalid" }), false);
});
```

Using `.test.cjs` avoids changing the root package to `"type": "module"` or adding TypeScript import-extension configuration. Keep the extracted module pure: erasable TypeScript only, relative imports, no `@/` aliases, JSX, Next runtime imports, or environment initialization. Node’s loader strips types but does not type-check, so normal `tsc`/build checks remain complementary.

Scope the test command to root files. A bare `node --test` could discover the Bun tests under `open-agents` and fail on `bun:test`.

## Existing conventions found

- `chatbot-template` has **no tests or test runner**:
  - `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\chatbot-template\package.json`
- `open-agents` consistently uses colocated `*.test.ts` files with `bun:test`:
  - Pure runtime-guard example:  
    `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\open-agents\apps\web\app\sessions\[sessionId]\chats\[chatId]\stream-recovery-policy.test.ts`
  - Small validation example:  
    `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\open-agents\apps\web\lib\github\repo-identifiers.test.ts`
  - Pure helper example:  
    `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\open-agents\packages\shared\lib\tool-state.test.ts`
  - Runner setup:  
    `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\open-agents\package.json`  
    `C:\Users\bijim\oxy-ai\open-agents\scripts\test-isolated.ts`

## Alternatives

- **Bun:** locally available as 1.3.10 and proven in `open-agents`, but the root declares pnpm, has no `@types/bun`, and does not declare or pin Bun. Do not introduce a second runtime solely for these tests.
- **Vitest/Jest/tsx:** none is declared or exposed as a root executable. Lockfile references inside dependencies or `open-agents` are transitive and should not be treated as available test infrastructure.
- If CI cannot guarantee a Node release with native TypeScript stripping, add a small explicit tool such as `tsx` later; Vitest would be unnecessary for a handful of pure guard tests.
</task_result>

I’m applying the hardening at two explicit trust boundaries: `POST /api/chat` will gain bounded parsing, deterministic loop/tool budgets, a wall-clock timeout, limited retries, and request-correlated lifecycle logs; `web_fetch` and search will gain bounded inputs, abortable network calls, response-size limits, and public-network-only URL validation across redirects. This stays inside `lib/ai` because a separate package would add ceremony before there is a second consumer; we can extract a runtime package during item 3 once persistence and Composio establish the real boundaries.

why are u installaing 
undici and ipaddr.js
**Evaluating undici necessity and alternatives****Preparing user choice on dependencies**

They were intended specifically to harden `web_fetch` against SSRF, because this app performs URL requests directly from the Next.js server, unlike Open Agents where fetching happens inside an isolated sandbox.

- `ipaddr.js`: reliably classifies IPv4 and IPv6 addresses so `web_fetch` can reject localhost, private networks, link-local addresses, cloud metadata endpoints, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 addresses.
- `undici`: provides a custom DNS lookup/dispatcher so the address validated by the application is the address actually contacted. A simple `dns.lookup()` followed by native `fetch()` leaves a DNS-rebinding gap.

No source code has been changed yet, but `package.json` and `pnpm-lock.yaml` now include them.

This is stronger network isolation, but probably too much dependency surface for the first pass. My recommendation is to **remove `undici`**, retain `ipaddr.js`, and use native DNS validation plus manual redirect validation. When the runtime later moves into an isolated worker or sandbox architecture, that becomes the stronger security boundary.

parts.text: **Summarizing architecture and build details****Documenting Phase 1 architecture and limits**

**Phase 1 Complete**
The existing runtime is now substantially more defensive without prematurely restructuring the project.

### Agent Runtime

`app/api/chat/route.ts` now enforces:

- Maximum request body: 256 KB
- Maximum conversation length: 64 messages
- Maximum agent steps: 5
- Maximum tool executions: 8
- Maximum output: 8,192 tokens
- One provider retry instead of the SDK default of two
- Total runtime timeout: 45 seconds
- Per-step timeout: 20 seconds
- Per-tool timeout: 15 seconds
- First-chunk and stalled-stream timeouts
- Request IDs returned through `x-request-id`
- Structured lifecycle logging for start, completion, cancellation, failure, and tool execution
- Sanitized client and server errors
- Input conversion error handling
- Prompt-injection guidance for untrusted web/tool content

A per-process concurrency admission limit was added in `lib/ai/runtime/concurrency.ts`:

- Defaults to four concurrent agent runs
- Configurable through `AGENT_MAX_CONCURRENT_REQUESTS`
- Configuration is capped at 20
- Returns `503` and `Retry-After: 5` when saturated
- Runtime slots are released idempotently on completion, failure, or cancellation

This concurrency limit protects an individual application process. It is not distributed rate limiting.

### Network Tools

`web_fetch` now has:

- Public HTTP/HTTPS URL enforcement
- Localhost, private, reserved, link-local, and metadata-address blocking
- IPv4, IPv6, and IPv4-mapped IPv6 classification using `ipaddr.js`
- DNS resolution checks before requests
- Validation of every redirect destination
- Maximum five redirects
- Credential-bearing URL rejection
- 12-second timeout with abort propagation
- 512 KB download limit
- 30,000-character tool-output limit
- Text-compatible content-type restrictions
- Bounded error-response reads
- Sanitized network errors

Search now has:

- Query and result-count bounds
- 10-second timeout behavior
- Abort propagation for DuckDuckGo
- 256 KB DuckDuckGo response limit
- Bounded titles, URLs, snippets, and synthesized answers
- Bounded errors from external search providers

There remains a small DNS time-of-check/time-of-use gap because native `fetch` performs its own DNS resolution after validation. Fully eliminating that requires a custom dispatcher or moving network tools into an isolated worker/sandbox. We deliberately avoided retaining `undici` for this phase.

### Tool Inputs

Schemas now bound:

- Clarification question count and text lengths
- Search query and result count
- URL and output lengths
- Composio app/action names
- Composio parameter payloads

Composio remains a non-executing stub as requested; no connection or execution behavior was introduced.

### Architecture

Keeping the runtime under `lib/ai/runtime/` is the correct boundary for now:

```text
lib/ai/
├── provider.ts
├── runtime/
│   ├── concurrency.ts
│   ├── network.ts
│   └── request.ts
└── tools/
```

A `packages/` workspace would currently add ceremony without another runtime consumer. During phase 3, package extraction will make sense if we introduce persistent jobs, background workers, reusable integration infrastructure, or a sandbox service.

### Verification

Added 12 focused tests covering:

- Request parsing and body limits
- Message-count limits
- Concurrency admission and release
- Public/private IP classification
- Unsafe URL rejection
- Redirect destination validation
- Bounded remote-response reading

All checks pass:

- `pnpm test`
- `pnpm typecheck`
- `pnpm lint`
- `pnpm build`

Lint now correctly excludes the two reference repositories. The pre-existing impure `Math.random()` sidebar skeleton behavior was also replaced with a deterministic width so root lint is clean.

Still deferred for later phases:

- Authentication
- Distributed rate limiting
- Persistent agent runs and resumable streams
- Usage accounting and spend limits
- Human approval for consequential Composio actions
- True network sandboxing
- Composio connection and entity/account management
